title: Single-nucleus atlas of cell-type specific genetic regulation in the human brain.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the Synapse REST API (Synapse is Sage Bionetworks' data-sharing platform) without logging in. Project syn61929918 'PsychAD_eQTL_release' has no access requirements and restrictionLevel OPEN, but anonymous canDownload=false and isEntityOpenData=false, so files need a logged-in Synapse account. Listed the results folder syn61929919: 12 summary tables (coloc, mashr, cell-type-specific eQTL, dynamic eQTL; about 108 MB in total) plus a cis_analysis folder of 34 per-cell-type parquet files totalling about 95.2 GB. Read the wiki's column preview (Source, Level, CellType, chr, start, end, variant, nonassessed_allele, ...).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 5.6M nuclei, 1,384 donors, 8 classes and 27 subclasses, 14,258 eGenes (genes with a detected eQTL), 2,073 dynamic eQTL genes and 1,655 trans-eQTL genes all come from the abstract and the Synapse wiki. Row counts, units and effect-size columns were not seen because no file could be downloaded. Paper has no PMCID (not open access in Europe PMC); the medRxiv preprint is in PMC (PMC11661307).

a1_downloadable.note: Summary statistics on Synapse (syn61929918) are tagged OPEN with no access application, but downloading needs a free Synapse login (checked via API: anonymous canDownload=false). Donor-level genotypes and snRNA-seq (single-nucleus RNA sequencing) data are on the AD Knowledge Portal and need a data-use agreement. Under the rubric, needing a login fails A1.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verified in files. Per the wiki, cis-eQTL (expression quantitative trait locus: a variant linked to gene expression) effects and cell-type-specificity calls are columns in the parquet and tsv files, so a label such as 'cell-type-specific eQTL yes/no' would not need constructing.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified. Rows carry rsIDs and coordinates, not sequences. Sequence inputs would have to be pulled from a reference genome, which is easy, but the build (presumably GRCh38) is not stated in the wiki preview.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns beyond the first 8 (effect size, standard error, p-value) were not seen. Units cannot be checked without downloading.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not counted. The paper reports 14,258 eGenes, and 981/857 cell-type-specific genes at class/subclass level, which is enough for classification if the tables match.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: about 108 MB of summary tables; full cis parquet set is about 95 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Sizes come from the Synapse API folder sums. A gene-level specificity task fits easily. Full variant-level cis results need per-file streaming.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not check. The abstract and Synapse wiki also disagree on which of 981/857 belongs to class vs subclass.

a8_label_provenance.note: eQTL effects are statistical estimates from measured genotypes and measured expression, not another model's predictions. The mashr (multivariate shrinkage method) specificity calls are model-derived, though, and would need care.

existing_models.name: scEEMS (single-cell Enhanced Expression Modifier Scores), CatBoost on 4,839 genomic features (medRxiv 2025.12.03.25341562)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; seen only as a search-result title and snippet. Predicts causal eQTL status for 6 brain cell types.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Enformer-style DNA sequence models (variant-effect scoring)
backbone.hardware: CPU for cached scores; GPU for scoring many variants

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx brain eQTLs; SingleBrain snRNA-seq eQTL meta-analysis (Nature Genetics 2026)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-model variant scores explain which bulk-tissue eQTLs are really driven by one brain cell type?

controls.positive_control: Known cell-type marker genes should show eQTLs in their own cell type (for example microglial AD (Alzheimer's disease) risk genes in microglia).
controls.external_validation: SingleBrain meta-analysis or the Emani et al. 2024 (Science) 388-brain single-cell eQTL set.

honest_claim_h3: Among eQTLs detectable in about 1,384 mostly older post-mortem prefrontal cortex donors, the model predicts which variant-gene effects are restricted to one cell type.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around a genetic variant to predict which brain cell types its effect on gene expression shows up in.
plain_idea.train_on: For each variant-gene pair, the DNA sequence around the variant (or a sequence model's score for it), labelled from the atlas tables. Row count unknown because the files could not be downloaded.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the variant's effect on expression is specific to a brain cell type, taken from the authors' statistical tests on single-nucleus RNA-seq and genotypes from 1,384 donors.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Statistical geneticists linking disease variants to cell types could rank candidate causal cell types for variants in donors or tissues never profiled.

ml_idea: Classify cell-type-specific versus shared cis-eQTLs from frozen DNA-model variant scores, holding out chromosomes, and test on SingleBrain.

effort.compute_note: Only the Synapse folder sizes were seen; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Create a free Synapse account, download specific_eQTL_class.tsv.gz, and count rows and columns, including effect-size units.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the openly licensed summary statistics on Synapse still need a logged-in account (anonymous download is refused), and donor-level data is controlled access on the AD Knowledge Portal. This is a free login, not an application, so it can be reopened if the user accepts a Synapse account. The task (cell-type-specific eQTL prediction) is also getting crowded.
